newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 12.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 12. Reuters has not verified these stories and does notvouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto has installed General Hartono as Indonesia's new information minister, replacing Harmoko, who now serves as the minister for special affairs. Suharto also installed General Wiranto as the army chief of staff in place of Hartono.
Economists have said Indonesia's economy will start recovering this year and reach sustainable growth in 1998, about a year behind the most developed countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
State-owned electricity company PLN will buy power from a new private power generator, PT Power Jawa Barat, at 6.04 U.S. cents per kilowatt hour (KWh) starting the year 2000.

A fact-finding team from the country's presidential advisory board has been sent to Banjarmasin in south Kalimantan to have a closer look at the political situation in the area after last month's deadly riots before the May 29 general elections. At least 124 people died in a shopping centre fire during the riot.

Indonesia's largest automobile manufacturer PT Astra International expects to post a net profit of 627 billion rupiah in 1997, up from 470 billion in 1996. Astra is poised to launch a compact Asia Family Car in the first quarter of 1998, two new models of Daihatsu sedans as well as one new Isuzu model.
PT Lippo General Insurance (LGI), a subsidiary of the Lippo Group, will soon offer up to 51 million, or 34 percent of its shares to the public.
